userStories.title: Add three non-default-blocking bot review trigger classes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add off-contract, version-skew and backend-fault to the shared bot finding vocabulary, review contract and configuration description without changing default blocking or the blocking predicate.

**Motivation** — The other kinds have no class, so they land in `normal`, and `normal` blocks.

**Approach** — The trigger vocabulary has one source, `FINDING_TRIGGERS` in `packages/nax/src/workflow/blocking-findings/index.ts`. The config schema (`z.enum(FINDING_TRIGGERS)`), the reply parser (`parseFindingTrigger`), the thread reader (`readFindingThreadFacts`) and the per-PR ruling parser (`effectiveBlockingTriggers`) all read it. Adding three members there makes all four accept the new classes with no further change.

`DEFAULT_BLOCKING_TRIGGERS` is not changed. `isBlockingFinding` is not changed. Every site that asks it (review posting, push-worthiness, readiness, carried findings, the chain notice, the fix facts) therefore treats a finding in a new class as it treats an `adversarial` finding today.

The rest is text:

1. The review contract in `bot-pr-review-builder.ts` gains one definition line per new class, one line that says what the evidence for `normal` is, and the three names in the finding shape.
2. The `bot.blockingTriggers` description in `config-descriptions.ts` names the three new classes.

The prompt text is facts, not orders. It defines the classes and says what the evidence for `normal` names. It says nothing about what a class does to readiness.

**Order.** The seven classes are listed in one order everywhere (the constant, the definition lines and the finding shape): `normal`, `off-contract`, `version-skew`, `backend-fault`, `own-concurrency`, `adversarial`, `manual`. The three new classes sit directly after `normal` because they are the conditions carved out of it. `manual` stays last, so the origin lines of #3008, which follow the `manual:` line, keep their place.

**Composition.** `isBlockingFinding` keeps its three tests in the same order: severity is `critical` or `important`; origin is not `fix-gap`; trigger is in the effective blocking set. A new class changes only which value the third test reads. A `critical` `version-skew` finding under the default set does not block. An `important` `off-contract` finding under a set that names `off-contract` blocks.

**Interface** — Symbols this feature only reads:

- `packages/nax/src/workflow/blocking-findings/index.ts`: `DEFAULT_BLOCKING_TRIGGERS: readonly FindingTrigger[]` (`["normal", "own-concurrency"]`), `parseFindingTrigger(value: unknown): FindingTrigger`, `isBlockingFinding(finding, blocking): boolean`, `readFindingThreadFacts(body): { severity; trigger; origin }`, `effectiveBlockingTriggers(input: EffectiveBlockingTriggersInput): EffectiveBlockingTriggers`.
- `packages/nax/src/config/schemas-bot.ts`: `BotConfigSchema`, whose `blockingTriggers` is `z.array(z.enum(FINDING_TRIGGERS)).min(1).default([...DEFAULT_BLOCKING_TRIGGERS])`.
- `packages/nax/src/operations/bot-pr-review-reply.ts`: `parsePrReviewReply`, whose findings carry `trigger: parseFindingTrigger(source.trigger)`.
- `packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts`: `postPrReview(input: PostReviewInput)`, which posts no inline thread for a finding `isBlockingFinding` rejects and lists it under `### Residual findings (not blocking)`.
- `packages/nax/src/bot/review-blocking.ts`: `hasPushWorthyItem(env: BotFixEnv): boolean`.

**Production targets** — Implement the targets, not the old vocabulary:

- `FINDING_TRIGGERS` (`packages/nax/src/workflow/blocking-findings/index.ts`): `["normal", "off-contract", "version-skew", "backend-fault", "own-concurrency", "adversarial", "manual"] as const`. `FindingTrigger` follows from it.
- `TRIGGER_CLASS_LINES` (`packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/bot-pr-review-builder.ts`): the lines below, in this order. The lead-in, `normal:`, `own-concurrency:`, `adversarial:` and `manual:` lines keep their exact text.

```text
Name each finding's class with "trigger" and the one detail that shows it with "triggerEvidence". The classes are:
normal: reachable in ordinary use of the product, as this repository documents or configures it.
For normal, "triggerEvidence" names the document, configuration, example or test in this repository that shows that use.
off-contract: needs a caller, subclass or configuration value that breaks a type, schema or documented contract of this repository.
version-skew: needs two versions of the product running together, or data written by an earlier version.
backend-fault: needs a store, network or clock failure between two steps of one operation.
own-concurrency: needs two of the tool's own processes or sessions interleaving.
adversarial: needs a deliberate actor (forged metadata, input the threat model excludes, shadowed builtins).
manual: needs a human acting on the checkout or state mid-operation.
```

- `FINDING_SHAPE` (same file): `"trigger": "normal|off-contract|version-skew|backend-fault|own-concurrency|adversarial|manual"`. The rest of the shape keeps its exact text.
- `FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS["bot.blockingTriggers"]` (`packages/nax/src/cli/config-descriptions.ts`): its first sentence reads `Finding trigger classes that can hold readiness: "normal", "off-contract", "version-skew", "backend-fault", "own-concurrency", "adversarial" or "manual" (default ["normal", "own-concurrency"]).` The sentences after it keep their exact text.

**Failure Handling** — Existing behavior, not additional test scope beyond the listed ACs:

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| A reply names a class outside the seven | `parseFindingTrigger` reads it `normal`, as today: the finding blocks. |
| A reply classes a finding `normal` with evidence that names no document, configuration, example or test | The finding is kept as `normal` and blocks. nax does not check the evidence text. |
| A thread, summary or artifact written before this change | It names one of the four earlier classes, which all remain members: read as before. |
| `bot.blockingTriggers` or a `blocking triggers:` comment names a new class | Accepted. Findings of that class hold readiness for that project or that PR. |
| A `minor` finding in a new class | Goes to `### Minor findings` as every minor does. |

Every row is behaviour the code already has. This feature changes none of it.

In this table, "blocks" and "hold readiness" retain the composition above: severity must be critical or important, origin must not be fix-gap, and the effective blocking set must include the trigger. The parser itself returns a class and never decides readiness. No unconditional blocking rule is introduced.

**Scope** — In: the four production targets above, including the CLI configuration description, existing unit and integration test updates, and the one new prompt-contract test file. Production schema, reply parsing, posting and push-worthiness entry points are exercised without changing their implementations. There are no inter-story exclusions because this feature has one story. Out: Changing `DEFAULT_BLOCKING_TRIGGERS`. It stays `["normal", "own-concurrency"]`; the three new classes do not hold readiness unless a project or a PR ruling names them (user ruling of 2026-11-23). A deterministic check of the evidence a reply gives for `normal`. nax keeps the class the reviewer names; the evidence line in the prompt is a definition, not a gate. Changing the severity scale line of the bot PR review contract. Changing the bot fix prompt (a definition of a finished fix, the standing of a reviewer suggestion). A separate change. Adding the new classes to the trigger vocabulary of the story, branch or acceptance reviewers. Only the bot PR review asks for a trigger. US-001 only: new tests for the Failure Handling rows beyond the listed acceptance criteria. Each row is behaviour the code already has and this feature does not change. Edits under `.nax/`, including this repository's own `.nax/config.json`. An operator who wants a new class to block adds it to `bot.blockingTriggers` by hand. Reclassifying findings already posted. Threads, summaries and artifacts written before this change keep the class they state. A class for test-strength findings (a test that would still pass without the change) or for documentation findings. Both stay in whichever class the reviewer names and block as they do today. Routing a fix-induced chain to the advisor, #2987 lever C. Changing the bot review or fix model in any operator config or profile. This is the reviewer side of #2987. #2987 stays open.

**Test placement and implementation sequence** — Use tdd-simple: add or update the listed acceptance tests before the vocabulary and exact-text implementation edits. Each new test goes beside the existing tests of the entry point it calls:

- `FINDING_TRIGGERS`, `DEFAULT_BLOCKING_TRIGGERS`, `parseFindingTrigger`, `isBlockingFinding`, `readFindingThreadFacts` and `effectiveBlockingTriggers`: `packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/blocking-findings.test.ts`.
- `BotConfigSchema`: `packages/nax/test/unit/config/bot-config.test.ts`.
- `parsePrReviewReply`: `packages/nax/test/unit/operations/bot-pr-review-reply.test.ts`.
- `buildBotPrReviewPrompt`: the new file under Creates. It declares its own minimal `BotPrReviewPromptInput` literal for a full code review; it shares no mock setup with another file.
- `postPrReview`: `packages/nax/test/integration/bot/post-blocking.test.ts`.
- `hasPushWorthyItem`: `packages/nax/test/unit/bot/review-blocking.test.ts`.
- `FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS`: `packages/nax/test/unit/cli/config-descriptions.test.ts`.

Some criteria are guards on the ruling, not new behaviour. The `DEFAULT_BLOCKING_TRIGGERS`, `isBlockingFinding`, `postPrReview` and `hasPushWorthyItem` criteria already hold at runtime on the code before this change, because `isBlockingFinding` only asks whether the class is in the set. Before the change their tests fail the test typecheck instead, since the new class names are not yet members of `FindingTrigger`. The criteria that fail at runtime before the change are the ones on `FINDING_TRIGGERS`, `parseFindingTrigger`, `readFindingThreadFacts`, `BotConfigSchema`, `effectiveBlockingTriggers`, `parsePrReviewReply`, `buildBotPrReviewPrompt` and `FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS`.

**Creates** — `packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/bot-pr-review-builder-trigger-classes.test.ts` — the contract ACs for the new class lines, the evidence line and their order. `bot-pr-review-builder.test.ts` is 614 lines, so these go in their own file by concern.

**Existing test modifications** — `packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/bot-pr-review-builder.test.ts` — the `taskContract` constant pins the whole contract text verbatim. It gains the `For normal, ...` evidence line directly after the `normal:` line, then the `off-contract:`, `version-skew:` and `backend-fault:` definition lines, and its finding shape line names the seven classes in the order `normal|off-contract|version-skew|backend-fault|own-concurrency|adversarial|manual`. Every other line of the constant keeps its exact text and order.

`packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/bot-pr-review-builder.test.ts` — test "AC-8 asks for a trigger class and its evidence in the finding shape" asserts the contract contains `"trigger": "normal|own-concurrency|adversarial|manual", "triggerEvidence": "..."`. It asserts the seven-class shape `"trigger": "normal|off-contract|version-skew|backend-fault|own-concurrency|adversarial|manual", "triggerEvidence": "..."` instead.

Use the existing `blocking()`, `callsTo()` and `summaryBody()` helpers for posting tests. Pass explicit blockingTriggers through blocking() overrides for the opt-in case, with no pre-existing own thread and origin absent or pr, so the assertion tests trigger membership rather than the existing-thread or fix-gap branches. For effectiveBlockingTriggers, supply the comment in comments with kind comment and its author in writers, plus configured: ["normal"]. For parsePrReviewReply, supply a serialized JSON reply with valid intent/quality and the finding, and empty threadIds/commentIds arrays; the exported API takes output text, not a reply object. The thread-facts body uses two actual newline characters before Trigger:, not literal backslash characters. The `findingItem()` helper fixes `trigger: "normal"`; override it with backend-fault and use origin pr for the push-worthiness AC. Supply the required set on env.review.blockingTriggers and make env.review.agreed contain only that finding: reviewBlockingTriggers reads the latest review's set before an older code review's or config's set.

**Seams** — None. The feature adds no exported symbol: it adds members to an existing exported constant, and the consumers that read that constant are exercised through their own entry points: `BotConfigSchema`, `effectiveBlockingTriggers`, `parsePrReviewReply`, `postPrReview` and `hasPushWorthyItem`.

[unit] isBlockingFinding for a critical finding with trigger version-skew, under blocking set ["normal", "own-concurrency"], returns false.
[unit] isBlockingFinding for an important finding with trigger off-contract, under blocking set ["normal", "off-contract"], returns true.

Trigger: backend-fault - the marker write fails after the body write" (where each

routing.reasoning: Four small production edits expand a shared tuple and exact prompt/help text; existing consumers already implement the required behavior. Multiple focused test suites guard the integration, but there are no new abstractions, dependencies, access-control changes or security-critical implementation paths.

analysis:
Existing enhancement, confined to @nathapp/nax (Bun, strict TypeScript, Zod, bun:test); no new dependencies or abstractions. Codebase-memory MCP was unavailable, so discovery used direct reads and text searches. Architecture guidance is indexed at docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:11 and its package/rule references apply during implementation. One binding story, US-001, runs in packages/nax with no dependencies.

Source changes: packages/nax/src/workflow/blocking-findings/index.ts:19 currently defines four FINDING_TRIGGERS; FindingTrigger is derived at :21. Expand only that constant to the seven ordered members. parseFindingTrigger at :38 already consults the constant and falls back to normal. DEFAULT_BLOCKING_TRIGGERS at :43 remains exactly normal and own-concurrency. isBlockingFinding at :63 already composes severity, origin and set membership in that order; retain its implementation. readFindingThreadFacts at :77 and its readTrigger helper at :92 flow through the parser. effectiveBlockingTriggers at :183 uses the same vocabulary through isFindingTrigger (:148) and parseScopeRuling (:153); existing writer authorization, top-level-comment restriction, newest-comment selection and invalid-ruling handling must not change. This feature does not modify access-control logic.

The other production edits are text-only within packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/bot-pr-review-builder.ts:263 (TRIGGER_CLASS_LINES), :279 (FINDING_SHAPE), and packages/nax/src/cli/config-descriptions.ts:68 (bot.blockingTriggers description). Add the evidence definition immediately after normal and the new definitions immediately before own-concurrency. Keep all seven names ordered identically in the constant, definition lines and finding shape. taskContract at bot-pr-review-builder.ts:293 shares the definitions between full and conversation-only reviews; origin definitions at :272 are conditionally appended after manual and must remain in place. Preserve every existing severity, origin and unrelated contract line exactly. Update only the first sentence of the config description; preserve its remaining residual-posting and collaborator-ruling sentences verbatim.

Consumers already accept the vocabulary centrally: packages/nax/src/config/schemas-bot.ts:13 builds blockingTriggers from z.enum(FINDING_TRIGGERS); packages/nax/src/operations/bot-pr-review-reply.ts:42 calls parseFindingTrigger for each finding and keeps optional evidence without checking that it names repository usage. These are read-only production entry points, tested in their own suites. packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts:440 delegates nonblocking selection to isBlockingFinding and :568 exports postPrReview. packages/nax/src/bot/review-blocking.ts:12 chooses the effective set from the newest review, older code review or config, while hasPushWorthyItem at :21 delegates finding membership to isBlockingFinding. Do not alter either production consumer. Other dependent sites found by search include bot/blocking-threads.ts:34, bot/carried-findings.ts:29, bot/carried-record.ts:22, bot/fix-carried.ts:2, bot/fix-facts.ts:23, bot/fix-report.ts:24, bot/convergence-summary.ts:16, bot/review-convergence.ts:12, bot/post-carried.ts:22, bot/carried-hold.ts:14, operations/bot-types.ts:1 and config/runtime-types-bot.ts:1. They inherit the enlarged type or membership checks without edits. Preserve the nested @/workflow/blocking-findings import boundary: its header (:6) explains that routing through the main workflow barrel would create config/operations cycles.

Tests and fixtures: packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/bot-pr-review-builder.test.ts:7 provides the minimal BotPrReviewPromptInput shape; :39 pins the whole taskContract and :536 starts the existing AC-8 shape assertion. Update both pins precisely, leaving every unrelated line unchanged. That file is 614 lines; put new contract-specific assertions into packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/bot-pr-review-builder-trigger-classes.test.ts, declaring a separate minimal input literal without importing sibling setup. packages/nax/test/integration/bot/post-blocking.test.ts:80 provides blocking(), :94 callsTo(), :102 summaryBody(), and :110 begins residual-posting coverage. Reuse those helpers for the three integration ACs, mocking forge calls and asserting inline endpoint calls versus summary text. packages/nax/test/unit/bot/review-blocking.test.ts:41 defines findingItem(origin) with trigger fixed to normal: construct the new backend-fault case by overriding trigger, rather than accidentally testing the helper's normal finding. Existing unit coverage is beside each entry point: workflow/blocking-findings.test.ts:48, :84, :93, :142 and :199; config/bot-config.test.ts:119; operations/bot-pr-review-reply.test.ts:82; cli/config-descriptions.test.ts:10.

Implementation/test sequence: write the specified ACs first in those existing suites plus the one new prompt suite; then make the vocabulary and exact text edits. Use tdd-simple because these are four small, established production changes with no new runtime mechanism. Some guards (defaults, membership, posting and push-worthiness) already behave correctly at runtime and fail pre-change only at test typecheck because FindingTrigger lacks the names; vocabulary, parser, schema, ruling, reply, prompt and description checks fail at runtime before implementation. Use package-scoped targeted bun test paths with --timeout=30000 during iteration; never bare bun test or bun run nax. Pipeline quality gates are not acceptance criteria. Do not run coverage in a nax sandbox.

Risk and compatibility: broadening the inferred union affects all typed consumers, but retaining the old four members preserves existing threads, summaries and artifacts without migration or rewriting. New classes are nonblocking by default, not hidden or discarded: critical/important findings are residual summary entries unless the effective config or per-PR set includes the class. Existing severity/origin gates still win, including fix-gap nonblocking behavior. No runtime evidence validator is introduced; normal remains the reported class even for ungrounded evidence. Unknown classes continue to parse as normal (and participate in existing blocking rules). Minor findings retain their existing summary section. The Failure Handling table documents existing behavior rather than extra implementation scope; retain it as design context and do not add tests beyond the listed US-001 ACs, as that story explicitly excludes them. No migration is required. Operators may opt into new blocking classes manually; implementation must not edit operator configs, profiles or other .nax files. The requested PRD artifact is the planning output, not a feature implementation change. This is only the reviewer side of #2987; #2987 stays open.

Refine audit: all 22 explicit spec acceptance criteria remain in US-001 in spec order, with the same conditions and assertions: (1) exact seven-member vocabulary/order; (2) unchanged two-member default; (3) off-contract parsing; (4) important off-contract nonblocking by default; (5) critical version-skew nonblocking by default; (6) important off-contract blocking when opted in; (7) backend-fault thread parsing from the exact two-newline body; (8) version-skew config parsing; (9) backend-fault writer ruling overrides config; (10) version-skew reply parsing; (11) exactly one exact off-contract definition; (12) exactly one exact version-skew definition; (13) exactly one exact backend-fault definition; (14) normal evidence line immediately follows normal; (15) seven definition lines in order; (16) exact seven-class finding shape/evidence fields; (17) conversation-only off-contract definition; (18) no inline post for default-nonblocking off-contract; (19) exact residual section, location prefix and trigger annotation; (20) inline post when off-contract is opted in; (21) backend-fault finding alone is not push-worthy under defaults; (22) exact config description prefix. No regression-qualifying clause was removed; no deprecated content-check tags occur. All assertions are observable through exported values, return values, generated prompt text or mocked forge writes. ACs 4, 5, 18 and 21 are existing negative-path requirements, so no new failure AC is needed. AC 2 protects backward compatibility of defaults; existing full-contract pins protect unrelated prompt text. The story description and ACs agree on unchanged defaults, severity/origin composition and explicit opt-in. Read-only interface signatures in the description are spec notation, not proposed exports or signature changes.

The five contextFiles match the spec's five recommended context files exactly; the only expectedFiles entry is the new prompt suite and is not context. US-001 has the binding workdir packages/nax and empty dependencies; no other stories or dependency references exist. Medium/tdd-simple remains the lightest realistic routing for four small production edits and existing-consumer test additions; no authentication, permissions or writer-role implementation is changed. All eleven feature exclusions remain verbatim in top-level outOfScope, including the US-001-specific prohibition on extra Failure Handling tests, which the spec places in its feature-level exclusion list. No exclusion has been promoted into an AC. The scope includes CLI description output and test updates, and excludes neither. Existing failure-table prose saying a finding blocks must be read with the unchanged severity/origin/membership conjunction, not as a request to make every parsed normal finding block regardless of those gates.
